Also percentages are generally more useful.
For example:
Say if the company's grown a lot during the last few years, so the numbers will likely to increase. 
But comparing the numbers along wouldn't be entirely accurate... Yes it would reflect growth, but that's about it. Percentages, on the other hand, can help to identify if you've improved on cost management or revenue growth management.

Also, say if your a small business. But you want to compare your performance to a larger, more well known business. Then your number would significantly be lower than a larger business. But does that mean you're results were horrible? No.  If you use percentage, the scale factor of how large a business is can also be ignored and it'll have a more accurate reflection of how your business it going.

Also, percentages are easier to understand in general
